requirements.text: An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation; no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA approved as a separate component and must carry the mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED PCB/lamp ESA for presence of the UN R10 approval mark.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.why: Defines the mandatory content of the approval mark affixed to the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circled E and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
requirements.why: Defines the mandatory content and layout of the approval mark affixed to the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for '10R-' followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall be laid out in accordance with the model in Annex 1, with dimension a = 6 mm min.
requirements.why: The mark on the ESA must follow the prescribed format and minimum size.
requirements.test_case: Measure the approval mark dimensions on the ESA and check a ≥ 6 mm.

requirements.text: The electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation shall have an approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. affixed to it, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.
requirements.why: The LED modules on PCB are an ESA intended for separate approval under R10 and must carry the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED PCB module (ESA) for presence of the UN R10 approval mark as per paragraph 5.3.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.why: The LED PCB of the rear lamp is an ESA fitted to an M1 vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC design (filtering, layout, grounding) and confirm the ESA passes all ESA EMC tests.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.why: The rear lamp's electronics are an ESA subject to component EMC approval.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that the test plan and report cover radiated and conducted emission and immunity tests for the LED module.

requirements.text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
requirements.why: Sets the binding test method for the lamp ESA's broadband emissions.
requirements.test_case: Perform a CISPR 25 ALSE broadband emission measurement per Annex 7 with the lamp in normal operation.

requirements.text: When measured using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband emission limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 6). In the 400 to 1,000 MHz band the limit shall be a constant 63 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.why: The LED driver electronics can generate broadband emissions.
requirements.test_case: Compare the quasi-peak (or peak minus 20 dB) broadband emission spectrum from 30 to 1,000 MHz against the limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for the lamp ESA's broadband emissions.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured broadband readings fall below the Annex 7 limit line.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
requirements.why: Sets the binding test method for the lamp ESA's narrowband emissions.
requirements.test_case: Perform a CISPR 25 ALSE narrowband emission measurement with an average detector per Annex 8.

requirements.text: When measured using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband emission limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 7). In the 400 to 1,000 MHz band the limit shall be a constant 53 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.why: The LED driver or controller may contain oscillators that produce narrowband emissions.
requirements.test_case: Compare the average-detector narrowband spectrum from 30 to 1,000 MHz against the limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for the lamp ESA's narrowband emissions.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured narrowband readings fall below the Annex 8 limit line.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed a pulse amplitude of +75 V / -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems, or +150 V / -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is supplied from the vehicle 12/24 V system and its functions are switched.
requirements.test_case: Measure switching transients on the lamp supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and check the peak amplitudes.

requirements.text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
requirements.why: The stop and position lamp functions of the ESA are immunity-related functions.
requirements.test_case: Perform ISO 11452 radiated immunity tests (ALSE, BCI, TEM, stripline or reverberation chamber) covering 20 to 6,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand, over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band, test levels of: stripline 60 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz). Over the whole band it shall withstand minimum test levels of: stripline 50 V/m; TEM cell 62,5 V/m; BCI 50 mA; ALSE 25 V/m below 2 GHz and 8 V/m above 2 GHz; reverberation chamber 18 V/m below 2 GHz and 6 V/m above 2 GHz.
requirements.why: These are the radiated immunity levels the lamp ESA must withstand.
requirements.test_case: Apply the Table 2a/2b severity levels for the chosen method and monitor the lamp output.

requirements.text: During the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, the ESA shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail criterion for the lamp's radiated immunity (unexpected stop light activation or lighting off).
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop and position lamp light output (e.g. with a camera or photodetector) for loss or unintended activation during exposure.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to the transient pulses conducted along 12/24 V supply lines according to ISO 7637-2: pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V) / -450 V (24 V), 500 pulses, FPSC III; pulse 2a at +37 V / +37 V, 500 pulses, FPSC I for immunity related functions (III otherwise); pulse 2b at +10 V / +20 V, 10 pulses, FPSC II (III otherwise); pulse 3a at -112 V / -150 V for 1 h, FPSC I (III otherwise); pulse 3b at +75 V / +150 V for 1 h, FPSC I (III otherwise).
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is supplied from the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the lamp supply inputs and assess functional status.

requirements.text: Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand the ISO 16750-2 starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V), 10 pulses, with functional status classification B for immunity related functions (for ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases) or C (for other ESA), and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.
requirements.why: A rear lamp for M1 vehicles may be fitted to ICE vehicles with a starter motor.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile level II ten times and classify the lamp's functional status per ISO 16750-1.

requirements.text: Where the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and Annex 8; otherwise the narrowband limits apply.
requirements.why: Determines whether narrowband testing is needed for the LED PCB.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED driver circuit for oscillators or switching regulators above 9 kHz.

requirements.text: An ESA with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and Annex 9.
requirements.why: Determines the applicability of radiated immunity testing to the lamp ESA.
requirements.test_case: Assess whether the lamp functions (stop and position lighting) are immunity related functions.

requirements.text: An ESA that is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.why: Determines the applicability of transient emission testing to the lamp ESA.
requirements.test_case: Review the lamp circuit for switches or inductive loads to decide whether ISO 7637-2 emission testing is required.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6; in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit remains constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.why: These are the broadband emission limits the LED PCB (ESA) must meet for type approval.
requirements.test_case: Compare the measured broadband radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz against the limit line of Appendix 6.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the broadband emission measurement.
requirements.why: This sets the operating condition of the LED PCB under which compliance with the limits must be shown.
requirements.test_case: Operate the LED PCB with all lamp functions energised at rated voltage/maximum load during the emission scan.

requirements.text: If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz; in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit remains constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.why: Defines the narrowband radiated emission limit line the lamp's ESA must meet.
requirements.test_case: Compare measured average-detector emission spectrum of the ESA against the limit line across 30-1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the narrowband emission test.
requirements.why: Constrains the operating condition of the lamp ESA under which emission limits must be met.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp with all functions (position, stop, reversing) energised at nominal voltage during the emission test.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand the test severity levels in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2a: Stripline 60 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).
requirements.why: Sets the radiated immunity test levels the lamp's LED PCB must withstand.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity test at the Table 2a levels for the selected method and confirm compliance over at least 90 % of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2b: Stripline 50 V/m (20 to 400 MHz); TEM cell 62,5 V/m (20 to 200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20 to 400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80 to 2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz); Reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF to 2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000 to 6,000 MHz).
requirements.why: Sets the minimum radiated immunity level over the full band for the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity test and confirm no frequency in 20 to 6,000 MHz falls below the Table 2b minimum levels for the selected method.

requirements.text: During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" of the ESA.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for the lamp ESA's radiated immunity.
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop, position and reversing lamp functions during radiated immunity testing and confirm no degradation of light output or function.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the radiated immunity tests.
requirements.why: Constrains the operating state of the lamp ESA during immunity testing.
requirements.test_case: Verify test report shows lamp functions energised in normal operating mode during exposure.

requirements.text: Radiated immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with test signal modulation AM 1 kHz 80 per cent depth in 20 to 400 MHz, PM2 (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) in 2,700 to 3,100 MHz, and PM3 (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) in 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.why: Defines the test signal conditions the ESA must be immune to.
requirements.test_case: Check test report frequency range and modulation settings against Annex 9 3.1.

requirements.text: Where the ESA (LED modules on PCB) does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and with Annex 8 (narrowband emission).
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA, and the presence of a switching driver or oscillator above 9 kHz decides whether narrowband emission testing applies.
requirements.test_case: Review the PCB schematic and BOM for oscillators, LED drivers or microcontrollers clocked above 9 kHz; if any are present, perform the narrowband emission test per Annex 8.

requirements.text: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is switched on its 12/24 V supply lines, so this exemption criterion decides whether transient conducted emission testing is needed.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the ESA circuit for switches, switched supply and inductive loads; if any are present, perform transient conducted emission testing per paragraph 6.7.

requirements.text: ESAs approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, in paragraph 7.
requirements.why: The LED module PCB is an ESA; every production unit must match the approved EMC type.
requirements.test_case: Perform CoP EMC tests on a series-production LED PCB sample against the paragraph 6 requirements and compare with the approved type.

requirements.text: Conformity of production of the ESA shall be checked on the basis of the data contained in the communication form(s) for type approval set out in Annex 3A and/or 3B, so production ESAs shall correspond to the data declared in that communication form.
requirements.why: Production ESAs are judged against the approved communication form data, so design changes outside it break CoP.
requirements.test_case: Compare series-production PCB configuration (layout, components, connector) against the type-approval communication form data.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified, the measured broadband and narrowband electromagnetic radiated emission levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits of paragraphs 6.5.2.1. (broadband: 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 63 dB microvolts/m in 400 to 1,000 MHz) and 6.6.2.1. (narrowband: 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in 30 to 75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in 75 to 400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 53 dB microvolts/m in 400 to 1,000 MHz).
requirements.why: The production LED driver PCB emits RF disturbances and must stay within the CoP emission tolerance.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband (Annex 7) and narrowband (Annex 8) radiated emissions of a series sample and check levels are within limit + 4 dB.

requirements.text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is verified, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength (or BCI current) up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.why: Production lamp electronics must keep signalling functions undisturbed under radiated fields at the CoP level.
requirements.test_case: Perform Annex 9 radiated immunity test on a series sample at 80 % of Table 2a/2b levels and monitor lamp functions (stop, position, reversing) for degradation.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified, the ESA shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions up to the conducted transient levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. (ISO 16750-2 starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b at the Table 3a/3b test levels, e.g. 12 V system: -75 V, +37 V, +10 V, -112 V, +75 V).
requirements.why: Production lamp ESA is connected to vehicle supply and must withstand conducted transients without loss of stop/position lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses and ISO 16750-2 starting profile to a series sample on its supply lines and verify functional status classification is met.

requirements.text: When the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is verified, the conducted transient emission of the ESA shall not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. (maximum pulse amplitude +75 V / -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems and +150 V / -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems).
requirements.why: The production LED driver circuit switches loads and must not inject transients above the allowed amplitudes.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions on the supply lines of a series sample per ISO 7637-2 and check pulse amplitudes against Table 1.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA (LED modules on PCB) shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
requirements.why: The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA and its broadband emissions are verified by this method.
requirements.test_case: Check that the EMC test plan and report reference CISPR 25 for the ESA broadband emission test.

requirements.text: During the broadband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load.
requirements.why: Defines the operating state in which the ESA must meet the emission limits.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp ESA with all functions (position, stop, reversing) energised at rated voltage during the emission scan and record this in the report.

requirements.text: For an ESA not involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is not a charging ESA, so the ALSE method applies to it.
requirements.test_case: Verify the lamp ESA was tested in an ALSE set-up per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4.

requirements.text: Ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1., except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
requirements.why: Valid compliance of the ESA's emissions depends on a sufficiently low ambient level.
requirements.test_case: Perform an ambient scan with the ESA off and confirm the noise floor is at least 6 dB below the 6.5.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits shall apply to the ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.why: Sets the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must comply with the emission limits.
requirements.test_case: Scan the ESA emissions from 30 MHz to 1,000 MHz and compare against the broadband limit.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits are for quasi-peak detectors; if peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
requirements.why: Determines the effective limit the ESA's measured emissions must meet.
requirements.test_case: Check detector type in the report and, for peak measurements, that the 20 dB correction was applied to the limit comparison.

requirements.text: The measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or scanning receiver using the parameters of Table 1 and Table 2 for 30 to 1,000 MHz: spectrum analyser peak RBW 100/120 kHz at -3 dB with minimum scan time 100 ms/MHz, quasi-peak RBW 120 kHz at -6 dB with minimum scan time 20 s/MHz; scanning receiver BW 120 kHz at -6 dB, maximum step size 60 kHz, minimum dwell time 5 ms (peak) and 1 s (quasi-peak); FFT-based instruments shall continuously record with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band.
requirements.why: Measurement parameters condition the validity of the ESA emission compliance result.
requirements.test_case: Review the receiver settings in the test report against Tables 1 and 2.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested, with the phase centre of the antenna in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.why: Defines the harness configuration of the lamp ESA during the emission test.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the test set-up photos to confirm LV harness is nearest the antenna and antenna centred on harness.

requirements.text: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation.
requirements.why: Determines whether an exceedance is attributed to the lamp ESA's non-compliance.
requirements.test_case: For any exceedance, repeat with ESA off to confirm whether the emission originates from the ESA.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.why: Defines the characteristic emission value of the ESA assessed against the limit.
requirements.test_case: Measure in both polarizations and evaluate the worst-case reading per band against the limit.

requirements.text: The narrowband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA and its narrowband emissions must be tested by this method.
requirements.test_case: Check that the ESA narrowband emission test report references CISPR 25.

requirements.text: The ESA narrowband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
requirements.why: Defines the test arrangement under which the lamp ESA's emissions are assessed.
requirements.test_case: Verify the test set-up is an ALSE per CISPR 25 clause 6.4, or an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4.

requirements.text: Measurements of ambient shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1., except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
requirements.why: Validity condition for the emission measurement of the lamp ESA.
requirements.test_case: Record an ambient scan with the ESA switched off and confirm it is at least 6 dB below the 6.6.2.1 limits.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits shall apply to the ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.why: Defines the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must meet the narrowband limits.
requirements.test_case: Scan radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare against the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limit line.

requirements.text: Narrowband emission measurements of the ESA shall be performed with an average detector.
requirements.why: The limit compliance of the lamp ESA is assessed with average-detector readings.
requirements.test_case: Check that the receiver is set to the average detector during the measurement.

requirements.text: The measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser (30 to 1,000 MHz, average detector: RBW at -3 dB 100/120 kHz, minimum scan time 100 ms/MHz) or a scanning receiver (30 to 1,000 MHz, average detector: BW at -6 dB 120 kHz, maximum step size 60 kHz, minimum dwell time 5 ms); FFT-based instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band.
requirements.why: Measurement parameters that condition the pass/fail result for the lamp ESA.
requirements.test_case: Verify instrument settings in the test report against Tables 1 and 2.

requirements.text: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.
requirements.why: Determines whether an exceedance is attributed to the lamp ESA as a failure.
requirements.test_case: For any exceedance, repeat with the ESA off to determine whether the emission originates from the ESA.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.why: Defines the reading used to judge the lamp ESA's compliance with the narrowband limits.
requirements.test_case: Measure in both antenna polarisations and evaluate the worst-case reading per band against the limit.

requirements.text: The ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the following radiated immunity test methods, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9: (a) absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
requirements.why: The LED PCB is an ESA whose radiated immunity must be demonstrated over the full range.
requirements.test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm the chosen method combination covers 20 to 6,000 MHz without gaps.

requirements.text: The test conditions for the ESA radiated immunity tests shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.why: Defines the conditions under which the lamp ESA must show immunity.
requirements.test_case: Verify the test report states compliance with ISO 11452-1 general conditions.

requirements.text: The ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, and shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA must remain functional while energised in normal operation during the test.
requirements.test_case: Operate the rear lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) during exposure and monitor for malfunction.

requirements.text: If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit, the interconnecting cables should ideally be the wiring harnesses as intended for use in the vehicle; if these are not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard, and all cables should be terminated as realistically as possible, preferably with real loads and actuators.
requirements.why: Harness configuration of the lamp ESA affects immunity results.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the test set-up for representative harness and loads.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps and dwell times according to ISO 11452-1, with test signal modulation of: (a) AM, 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz range; (b) PM2, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz range; (c) PM3, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
requirements.why: Sets the frequency range and modulation the ESA must withstand.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity sweep 20–6,000 MHz with specified modulations and confirm no lamp malfunction.

requirements.text: If the ESA fails the tests defined in Annex 9, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
requirements.why: Determines the validity of a failure verdict for the lamp ESA.
requirements.test_case: On any failure, check field calibration/monitoring to confirm the failure was under controlled conditions.

requirements.text: When the absorber chamber test is used, the test field conditions shall be established by the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2 and the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
requirements.why: Test condition the lamp ESA must pass if the absorber chamber method is used.
requirements.test_case: Perform ALSE test per ISO 11452-2 with substitution method and vertical polarisation.

requirements.text: When TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3, using the method of maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell.
requirements.why: Test condition the lamp ESA must pass if the TEM cell method is used.
requirements.test_case: Perform TEM cell test per ISO 11452-3 with maximum coupling orientation.

requirements.text: When bulk current injection testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench with either the substitution method and the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA, or the closed loop method and the injection probe at 900 mm from the ESA; alternatively, in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with the substitution method and injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA.
requirements.why: Test condition the lamp ESA must pass if BCI is used.
requirements.test_case: Perform BCI test with probe at the specified distance and verify lamp operation.

requirements.text: When stripline testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
requirements.why: Test condition the lamp ESA must pass if stripline is used.
requirements.test_case: Perform stripline test per ISO 11452-5 on the lamp harness.

requirements.text: When the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11, using a test setup with ground plane unless otherwise specified.
requirements.why: Test condition the lamp ESA must pass if the reverberation chamber is used.
requirements.test_case: Perform reverberation chamber test per ISO 11452-11 with ground plane.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply and shall limit the conducted transients it generates on the vehicle power supply.
requirements.why: The lamp PCB is an ESA connected to the 12/24 V vehicle supply.
requirements.test_case: Perform ISO 7637-2 immunity and emission tests on the lamp PCB supply lines and verify pass criteria.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.why: The lamp ESA is supplied from 12/24 V lines subject to transient immunity requirements.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b to the lamp supply and connected lines and check functional status.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, unless the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor.
requirements.why: The M1 rear lamp ESA is not restricted to electric vehicles, so the starting profile applies.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines and verify correct lamp operation.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines and other connections operationally connected to supply lines shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 and shall comply with the applicable limits.
requirements.why: The lamp PCB may generate switching transients onto the vehicle supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Measure transient conducted emissions of the lamp PCB on supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare with limits.

requirements.text: The rear lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.why: General installation obligation applying to every lamp function of the rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Vibration test of the mounted lamp followed by photometric and aim re-verification.

requirements.text: It shall not be possible for the rear lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
requirements.why: Applies to the lamp attachment (fasteners, housing bosses) maintaining aim.
requirements.test_case: Inspect fasteners/clips and mounting design for positive location preventing inadvertent misalignment.

requirements.text: The reference axis of each light-signalling function of the rear lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road and parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° in each direction.
requirements.why: Rear position, stop, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflector are light-signalling devices fitted to the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the installed lamp reference axis orientation relative to the ground plane and median longitudinal plane.

requirements.text: Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the rear lamp laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
requirements.why: Binds the installation of the product per its fitting instructions.
requirements.test_case: Check installation against the lamp manufacturer's fitting instructions.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the normal condition of use.
requirements.why: Test condition constraining verification of lamp position and orientation.
requirements.test_case: Measure lamp height and orientation on unladen vehicle on a flat horizontal surface.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp.
requirements.why: Rear lamps are fitted as left/right pairs.
requirements.test_case: Measure left and right lamp positions relative to the vehicle median plane.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane (not applicable to the interior structure of the lamp).
requirements.why: Left/right rear lamp variants must be mirror symmetrical.
requirements.test_case: Compare exterior geometry of left and right lamps for mirror symmetry.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
requirements.why: Paired rear lamps emit red and white light which must match colorimetrically.
requirements.test_case: Measure chromaticity of each function on left and right lamps.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, rear lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
requirements.why: Paired rear lamps must have matching photometry.
requirements.test_case: Compare photometric distributions of left and right lamps for each function.

requirements.text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the pair requirements for the rear lamps shall be satisfied so far as is possible.
requirements.why: Applies to the paired rear lamp installation on the M1 vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Review installation on asymmetrical vehicle body for best achievable symmetry.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements shall be fulfilled.
requirements.why: The rear lamp groups several functions in one housing.
requirements.test_case: Verify each function of the multi-function lamp individually against its colour, position, visibility and wiring requirements.

requirements.text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each lamp function shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
requirements.why: Grouped multi-function rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Photometric and colorimetric measurement of each function with all other functions OFF.

requirements.text: When the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions (e.g. stop lamp) which can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
requirements.why: Rear position and stop lamps share LED/lens and can be ON together.
requirements.test_case: Measure stop lamp chromaticity with the rear position lamp simultaneously ON.

requirements.text: Where a single lamp's apparent surface is composed of two or more distinct parts, either the total projected area of the distinct parts shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or the minimum distance between facing edges of two adjacent distinct parts shall not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicularly to the reference axis (not applicable to a single retro-reflector).
requirements.why: LED-array functions may have apparent surfaces composed of distinct parts.
requirements.test_case: Measure projected apparent surface areas and gaps between distinct parts in the reference axis direction.

requirements.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of each rear lamp function shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.
requirements.why: Applies to the steady-burning rear position, stop and reversing lamps.
requirements.test_case: Monitor intensity and colour over time with each function ON.

requirements.text: When the photometric characteristics of a rear lamp function vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is used to provide another lighting function, any variation shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
requirements.why: Shared LEDs between rear position and stop functions may vary intensity.
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry in each operating mode (e.g. position+stop) against the device limits.

requirements.text: Red light emitted by the rear lamp shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
requirements.why: The rear lamp emits red light (rear position, stop, retro-reflector).
requirements.test_case: Visibility check from the front of the vehicle.

requirements.text: There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red rear lamp functions if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (Annex 4).
requirements.why: Verification criterion for red light of the rear lamp towards the front.
requirements.test_case: Observe from Zone 1 (1 m to 2.2 m height, 15° outward planes) at 25 m ahead of the vehicle.

requirements.text: In case of doubt, the red light emitted to the front by the rear lamp shall be not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
requirements.why: Quantitative limit for red light from the rear lamp visible forward.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity of red light towards the front with goniophotometer.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, end-outline marker lamps and side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp, except when switched ON as parking lamps or the other conditions of paragraph 5.11.1 exist.
requirements.why: The rear position lamp function is wired into the position lamp circuit.
requirements.test_case: Functional check of lighting switch activating all position lamp circuits simultaneously.

requirements.text: The rear lamp shall not be concealed.
requirements.why: Concealment is prohibited for all lamps except headlamps and front fog lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that no concealment device covers the rear lamp.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.why: Product includes a rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of rear position lamp chromaticity coordinates.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.why: Product includes a stop lamp.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of stop lamp chromaticity coordinates.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.why: Product includes a reversing lamp behind a red-tinted outer lens window area.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of reversing lamp chromaticity through its lens window.

requirements.text: The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
requirements.why: Product includes a rear retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of retro-reflected light.

requirements.text: The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
requirements.why: Applies to each function provided by the rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Count installed functions on the vehicle.

requirements.text: Where the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector is installed on a movable component, at all fixed positions of the movable component it shall meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.
requirements.why: Applies if the rear lamp is mounted on a tailgate/boot lid.
requirements.test_case: Verify position, visibility and photometry at every fixed position of the movable component.

requirements.text: When the movable components are in a position other than the normal position of use, the rear lamp devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.
requirements.why: Applies if the rear lamp is mounted on a movable component.
requirements.test_case: Assess lamp light output with movable component open.

requirements.text: When the rear lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the normal position(s) of use, the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.why: Applies if the rear lamp is mounted on a movable component.
requirements.test_case: Cycle the movable component and measure lamp position/aim after return.

requirements.text: The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component in any fixed position different from the normal position of use; otherwise additional lamps meeting all position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements shall be switched ON.
requirements.why: Rear position lamp and retro-reflector are covered by the hiding limit.
requirements.test_case: Measure obscured fraction of apparent surface with movable components in each fixed position.

requirements.text: With the exception of the retro-reflector, each rear lamp function shall be capable of being made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse, otherwise it is deemed not to be present.
requirements.why: Determines whether rear lamp functions count as present on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Functional check that each function operates when installed with its fuse.

requirements.text: Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the rear position lamp function is provided, the replacement function shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the failed function, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function, and a tell-tale on the dashboard shall indicate the temporary replacement and need for repair.
requirements.why: Applies if the rear position lamp uses a fail-safe substitution strategy.
requirements.test_case: Simulate rear position lamp failure and check replacement colour, intensity, position and tell-tale.

requirements.text: There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of each rear lamp function observed from infinity.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility applies to rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Check geometric visibility angles of the installed lamp for obstruction by body parts.

requirements.text: If, when the rear lamp is installed, any part of its apparent surface is hidden by further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
requirements.why: Applies to partially obscured installed rear lamp functions.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of the lamp with the vehicle obstruction simulated.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in paragraph 6 when installed on a vehicle.
requirements.why: Each function of the rear lamp requires device type approval (R148/R150).
requirements.test_case: Check approval markings and certificates of each function.

requirements.text: When a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with it, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
requirements.why: The rear position lamp and stop lamp may share LED modules and can be ON simultaneously.
requirements.test_case: Switch ON the rear position lamp together with the reciprocally incorporated function (e.g. stop lamp) and measure the chromaticity of that function.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall not be reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator lamp.
requirements.why: The product contains a stop lamp, which is subject to this prohibition.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the design to confirm the stop lamp does not share light sources/apparent surface with any direction-indicator function.

requirements.text: Where a single lamp of the rear lamp (as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(a)) has an apparent surface composed of two or more distinct parts, it shall be installed such that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing that projection, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis; these requirements do not apply to a single retro-reflector.
requirements.why: The LED array/reflector cells may produce an apparent surface composed of distinct parts for a lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Project the apparent surface parts along the reference axis and check the 60 % area ratio of the circumscribing quadrilateral or the ≤ 75 mm gap between facing edges.

requirements.text: Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included in the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system.
requirements.why: The rear lamp contains several lamps and apparent surfaces in one housing with a common outer lens.
requirements.test_case: Review the design/approval documentation to confirm the functions sharing the common housing and outer lens are not treated as an interdependent lamp system.

requirements.text: The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle (rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors) shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
requirements.why: The rear lamp provides rear position, stop, reversing and retro-reflector functions whose installed number on the M1 vehicle must match R48's individual specifications.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle installation and count each installed function against the number required in the individual specifications of paragraph 6.

requirements.text: There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) observed from infinity; obstacles already present when the lamp was type-approved are not taken into account.
requirements.why: Every installed lamp function of the rear lamp must have unobstructed geometric visibility.
requirements.test_case: Check on the vehicle installation (CAD/physical) that no body part intrudes into the geometric visibility angles of each lamp's apparent surface viewed from infinity.

requirements.text: If geometric visibility measurements are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.
requirements.why: Constrains how the rear lamp's geometric visibility is verified as installed.
requirements.test_case: Verify the visibility measurement set-up uses parallel-shifted observation directions when measuring at short distance.

requirements.text: If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
requirements.why: Partial masking by vehicle parts must not cause the rear lamp functions to fall below their approval photometry.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of the installed lamp with the obscured portion masked, compared against the device approval values.

requirements.text: When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal is reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground, measured from the H plane), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
requirements.why: Defines the photometric field the installed rear lamp must satisfy depending on its mounting height.
requirements.test_case: Measure the H-plane height of the installed lamp; if below 750 mm, verify photometry over the field down to 5° below horizontal.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp is mandatory on motor vehicles.
requirements.why: M1 is a motor vehicle and P-03 is its reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle to confirm that at least one reversing lamp is fitted.

requirements.text: For motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device shall be mandatory and a second device is optional.
requirements.why: Sets the permitted number of reversing lamps on the M1 vehicle carrying P-03.
requirements.test_case: Count the reversing lamps installed on the M1 vehicle and confirm there are one or two.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.why: P-03 must carry a device approval under R23 or R148.
requirements.test_case: Verify the R23 or R148 approval marking on the reversing lamp.

requirements.text: In height, the reversing lamp shall be installed not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
requirements.why: Mounting height constraint for P-03 on an M1 vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the illuminating surface above the ground in the installed position.

requirements.text: In length, the reversing lamp shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: The rear lamp housing P-03 is mounted on the rear exterior.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installation position of the lamp on the vehicle.

requirements.text: For a reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility shall be defined by angles α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, and β = 45° to the right and to the left if there is only one device, or 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices.
requirements.why: The drawing callout 'visible to 45° outboard' relates to P-03's geometric visibility.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the apparent surface of the lamp is visible over the specified α and β angles in the installed position.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.why: Orientation requirement for P-03.
requirements.test_case: Check that the reference axis of the installed lamp points rearwards.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the reversing lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
requirements.why: Switching logic constraint for the P-03 reversing lamp and its electrical connection.
requirements.test_case: Functionally check that the lamp lights only with reverse gear engaged and the propulsion system enabled.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the propulsion start/stop control is not in a position permitting operation of the propulsion system.
requirements.why: Switch-off condition for the P-03 reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: Disengage reverse gear or switch off the propulsion system and confirm the lamp turns OFF and cannot be switched ON.

requirements.text: A tell-tale for the reversing lamp is optional; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
requirements.why: May require P-03 and its electronics to provide a failure signal.
requirements.test_case: Check the R23/R148 component requirements and verify that a failure tell-tale is provided if required.

requirements.text: Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be present (mandatory on all categories of vehicles, including M1).
requirements.why: The product's stop lamp function is an S1/S2 device mandatory on M1 vehicles.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle installation to confirm S1/S2 stop lamps are fitted.

requirements.text: Two S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be installed on the vehicle.
requirements.why: The rear lamp provides one of the two required S1/S2 stop lamps.
requirements.test_case: Count the S1/S2 stop lamps fitted on the vehicle rear (one per side).

requirements.text: The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.why: The stop lamp in the product must hold the component approval required for installation.
requirements.test_case: Verify the stop lamp carries a valid R7 (02+) or R148 (00+) approval mark.

requirements.text: For M1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Width position constraint applies to the product's S1/S2 stop lamp on an M1 vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lateral distance from the outermost point of the apparent surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge (≤ 400 mm).

requirements.text: S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be mounted not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
requirements.why: Height constraint applies to the product's S1/S2 stop lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the apparent surface above ground on the vehicle (350–1,500 mm, or up to 2,100 mm where justified).

requirements.text: S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Length position constraint for the product's S1/S2 stop lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed position on the vehicle rear.

requirements.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall provide a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle; for stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility requirement binds the lamp's optical design and installation.
requirements.test_case: Verify the apparent surface is visible over 45° outward and 45° inward (20° inward below H plane if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The S1 or S2 category stop lamp shall provide a vertical geometric visibility angle of 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.why: Vertical visibility requirement binds the lamp's optical design and installation.
requirements.test_case: Verify visibility of the apparent surface over 15° up and 15° down (5° down if mounted below 750 mm).

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Orientation applies to the installed stop lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the reference axis orientation of the installed lamp.

requirements.text: All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
requirements.why: Electrical connection requirement for the product's stop lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Apply the service brake and verify all stop lamps illuminate simultaneously.

requirements.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp shall be provided if required by the component regulation (otherwise the tell-tale is optional).
requirements.why: May require failure-detection capability in the stop lamp electronics.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the component regulation requires a failure tell-tale and, if so, verify its operation on simulated stop lamp failure.

requirements.text: The rear position lamps (devices of R or R1 or R2 categories) shall be mandatory on the vehicle.
requirements.why: The product provides the mandatory rear position lamp function for an M1 vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle to confirm rear position lamps are fitted.

requirements.text: Two rear position lamps shall be installed, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.why: The lamp must carry a valid R7/R148 approval to be installed as a rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Count the installed rear position lamps and check their approval markings against R7 (02 series or later) or R148.

requirements.text: In width, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Constrains the lateral mounting position of the rear position lamp on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lateral distance from the outermost point of the apparent surface to the vehicle's extreme outer edge.

requirements.text: In height, the rear position lamp shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).
requirements.why: Constrains the vertical mounting position of the rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure the height of the apparent surface above the ground on the unladen vehicle.

requirements.text: In length, the rear position lamp shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Defines the longitudinal mounting position of the product.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp's longitudinal location on the vehicle.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° inwards and 80° outwards; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
requirements.why: The lamp design and installation must provide the required horizontal visibility.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility of the apparent surface over the horizontal angular field with the lamp installed.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal; where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.why: The lamp design and installation must provide the required vertical visibility.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed visibility of the apparent surface over the vertical angular field with the lamp installed.

requirements.text: For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1 and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm) and a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle may be reduced to 5° where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm).
requirements.why: Alternative visibility field applicable to M1 vehicles with rear side-marker lamps.
requirements.test_case: If a rear side-marker lamp is fitted and this alternative is chosen, verify visibility over the reduced angular field.

requirements.text: To be considered visible, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light being excluded.
requirements.why: The lamp incorporates a retro-reflector whose area cannot count towards the visible apparent surface.
requirements.test_case: Measure the unobstructed projected apparent surface (excluding the non-transmitting retro-reflector area) at the boundary angles and confirm ≥12.5 cm².

requirements.text: The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.why: Constrains the installed orientation of the product.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the orientation of the lamp's reference axis on the vehicle.

requirements.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
requirements.why: The rear position lamp's electrical connection must follow paragraph 5.11.
requirements.test_case: Operate the position lamp switch and verify all listed lamps switch ON and OFF together.

requirements.text: A closed-circuit tell-tale shall be mandatory for the rear position lamps and shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this requirement does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
requirements.why: Installation of the rear position lamp function requires a tell-tale.
requirements.test_case: Switch on position lamps and verify the combined tell-tale operates.

requirements.text: A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
requirements.why: LED rear position lamps may require failure indication under the component Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Simulate lamp failure and verify the failure tell-tale operates where the component Regulation requires it.

requirements.text: The rear non-triangular retro-reflector shall be fitted (mandatory) on the M1 motor vehicle.
requirements.why: Presence is mandatory on motor vehicles including M1.
requirements.test_case: Inspect vehicle rear for presence of rear retro-reflectors.

requirements.text: The number of rear non-triangular retro-reflectors shall be two, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.
requirements.why: The P-05 retro-reflector must be a type-approved Class IA/IB device, one per side.
requirements.test_case: Verify two retro-reflectors fitted and check their Class IA/IB approval markings per R3 or R150.

requirements.text: Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
requirements.why: Condition binding any extra retro-reflecting elements integrated in the rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect any additional retro-reflecting devices for interference with mandatory lamps.

requirements.text: In width, that point on the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Width position limit applies to the retro-reflector on M1.
requirements.test_case: Measure lateral distance from outermost illuminating surface point to vehicle outer edge (≤ 400 mm).

requirements.text: In height, the retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
requirements.why: Mounting height limits bind the retro-reflector grouped in the rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Measure height of the illuminating surface above ground at unladen condition.

requirements.text: In length, the retro-reflector shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.
requirements.why: Longitudinal position requirement for the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Inspect installation position at vehicle rear.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall have geometric visibility of horizontal angle 30° inwards and outwards and vertical angle 10° above and below horizontal; where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured from the H plane according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility angles constrain the retro-reflector design and installation.
requirements.test_case: Verify unobstructed view of the illuminating surface over the prescribed angular field on the vehicle.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.
requirements.why: Orientation requirement for the installed retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Inspect orientation of the retro-reflector reference axis towards the rear.

requirements.text: Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6.; the installed rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the rear retro-reflector shall therefore conform in production to the approved installation requirements.
requirements.why: The installed rear lamp functions must keep meeting the paragraph 5 and 6 installation requirements on every production vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Conformity-of-production audit of series vehicles verifying the installed rear lamp against the approved installation requirements of paragraphs 5 and 6.

requirements.text: The position of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector in width, in height and in length shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled, when checked in accordance with paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4.
requirements.why: Lamp mounting position on the vehicle is verified during CoP and must meet the individual lamp specifications.
requirements.test_case: Measure the position of the installed lamp on production vehicles and compare it with the individual position specifications.

requirements.text: The angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, with an allowance on the angle limits corresponding to the ±3° mounting variation permitted in paragraph 5.3.
requirements.why: Geometric visibility of the rear lamp functions is a pass/fail CoP check.
requirements.test_case: Check the geometric visibility angles of the installed lamp per paragraph 2.10.7 and confirm they lie within specification ±3°.

requirements.text: The rear lamp shall not make red light visible towards the front, and the white light of the reversing lamp shall be visible towards the rear only as permitted, when checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10.
requirements.why: The red rear lamps and white reversing lamp must satisfy the colour-direction visibility checks.
requirements.test_case: Visually check from the front for red light and from the rear for white light per paragraph 5.10.

requirements.text: When every lamp is switched on through the vehicle electrical system, the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp and their associated tell-tales shall function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
requirements.why: Electrical connection and functioning of the rear lamp functions are verified in CoP.
requirements.test_case: Switch on each lamp function on the vehicle and verify correct operation and tell-tale behaviour.

requirements.text: The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors shall fulfil the requirements of paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, as checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.
requirements.why: The lamp's colour, category and markings are inspected for conformity during CoP.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the installed lamps and their approval markings for presence, number, colour, arrangement and category.

requirements.text: For verifying that no red light is visible to the front and no white light (other than from the reversing lamp) is visible to the rear, zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground. In width they shall be bounded by two vertical planes forming, to the front and to the rear respectively, an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane. These planes pass through the point(s) of contact of vertical planes parallel to the median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width; where there are several points of contact, the foremost corresponds to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.
requirements.why: Defines the visibility zones in which the lamp's red and white light emission and reflections must comply with §5.10.1/5.10.2 for the installed rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: With the rear lamp installed on the vehicle, observe from all eye positions within zone 2 (1 m to 2.2 m high, 15° outward planes behind the vehicle). Verify that the only directly or indirectly visible white light comes from the reversing lamp, and that no red light from the lamp is visible within zone 1 to the front.

requirements.text: Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.why: The rear lamp is a device type-approved under R148 and must provide marking space.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp drawing and sample for a marking area large enough for all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.why: Applies to all markings the rear lamp carries.
requirements.test_case: Visually check legibility and perform a rub/durability test on the markings.

requirements.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.why: The rear lamp carries an approval marking whose size is constrained.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval mark on the lamp; it must be at least 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.why: Defines the mandatory content of the lamp's approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number, and this sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.why: Mandatory content and placement of the lamp's approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Check the marking includes a 4-6 digit sequential number located next to the circled E.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4. (R1 or R2 for the rear position lamp, S1 or S2 for the stop lamp, AR for the reversing lamp).
requirements.why: The lamp contains rear position, stop and reversing functions which must be identified by symbols.
requirements.test_case: Verify the presence of the correct function symbols for each lamp function in the marking.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. 148R01).
requirements.why: Mandatory content of the lamp's approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '148R' followed by the series digits.

requirements.text: On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.why: A rear combination lamp is typically side-specific and must indicate its mounting position.
requirements.test_case: For a handed (left/right) lamp, check for a horizontal arrow in the marking.
