requirements.test_case: Perform the water immersion test, followed by the n-heptane/toluol wipe and the detergent oil wipe, with inspection after each.

requirements.text: Where necessary, the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6 and then to the abrasive-strength test of its rear face in Part 5 of Annex 6.
requirements.why: Applies to the retro-reflector, including when it is combined with the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Perform the salt mist test (2 × 24 h) and the rear-face nylon brush plus fuel test, then measure RI.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
requirements.why: The exterior PMMA retro-reflector is exposed to UV and weather.
requirements.test_case: Expose the retro-reflector for 500 h of accelerated weathering per EN ISO 4892-2, then check colour and RI.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
requirements.why: This is the post-test colour criterion for the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Measure night-time colour coordinates after each test group.

requirements.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have an RI which satisfies the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4., verified for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.why: This is the post-test photometric criterion for the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° after each test group and compare it with Table 3.

requirements.text: Where more than one axis of reference, or a range of axes of reference, is specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements for each specified axis of reference or for the extreme axes of the specified range.
requirements.why: Compliance must hold for every declared mounting reference axis of the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements for each declared axis of reference or each extreme axis.

requirements.text: For photometric measurements of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered, and the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2.
requirements.why: This constrains the effective optical area of the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Mask the device to the declared perimeter, which lies within a 200 mm circle and does not exceed 100 cm2, before measuring.

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than the following values in mcd·lx^-1: at an angle of divergence of 20', 3.00∙10^2 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.00∙10^2 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and 1.00∙10^2 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°; at an angle of divergence of 1°30', 5 at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 2.8 at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and 2.5 at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°.
requirements.why: These are the minimum photometric values for the red rear retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric RI measurement under CIE Illuminant A at all Table 3 angles.

requirements.text: RI values lower than those shown in the last applicable columns of Table 3 shall not occur within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
requirements.why: This is a photometric uniformity constraint on the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Scan RI within the bounded solid angle and confirm no value falls below the minimum.

requirements.text: Where the Class IA or IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.why: This condition depends on the rear lamp's mounting height on the M1 vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit downward measurements to 5° if it is below 750 mm.

requirements.text: The night-time colour of the retro-reflector shall be tested according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
requirements.why: This defines the colour verification condition for the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Perform night-time colour measurement per paragraph 4.2.1.

requirements.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.why: The rear retro-reflector must reflect red light.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reflected light chromaticity and compare it with the R48 red boundaries.

requirements.text: After the heat test of 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C, the retro-reflector shall show no distortion on visual inspection, and the tests shall be performed in the chronological order of Table 4 for Classes IA and IB.
requirements.why: This is the heat resistance and test sequence for the moulded plastic retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect for distortion after the heat test and follow the Table 4 sequence.

requirements.text: After the water test (10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position), the fuel test (5 min) and the oil test (5 min), the retro-reflector shall pass visual inspection and shall meet colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.why: These are the environmental resistance criteria of Table 4 applicable to the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Sequential water, fuel and oil tests, each followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and RI measurement at 20'.

requirements.text: After the corrosion test (24 h, 2 h interval, 24 h) and the rear-face test (1 min), the retro-reflector shall pass visual inspection and shall meet colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.why: These are the corrosion and rear-face resistance criteria of Table 4 for the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Perform the salt mist and rear-face tests, followed by visual inspection and RI measurement at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

requirements.text: When the RI of the retro-reflector is measured at β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be checked by slightly turning the device whether any mirror effect is produced; if there is any such effect, the RI reading shall be taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
requirements.why: Defines the illumination angle at which the retro-reflector's RI is assessed against the limits.
requirements.test_case: Turn the device slightly at β1 = β2 = 0° on the goniometer to check for a mirror effect. If one is seen, measure RI at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° and compare with the paragraph 5 limits.

requirements.text: With β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and a divergence angle of 20', a retro-reflector not marked "TOP" rotated about its axis of reference to the position of minimum RI shall conform to the RI value specified in paragraph 5. The RI at the other illumination and divergence angles shall be measured in that position of ε, and the device may be rotated ±5° from that position only if the specified values are not attained.
requirements.why: The RI pass/fail criterion applies to the product's retro-reflector in its worst rotational orientation.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the device about its reference axis to find minimum RI at 20' divergence and verify it meets the paragraph 5 value. Measure the other angles at that ε, using ±5° if needed.

requirements.text: With β1 = β2 = 0° (or the specified angle) and a divergence angle of 20', a retro-reflector marked "TOP" shall not fall below the prescribed RI value in any position assumed during rotation about its axis of ±5°.
requirements.why: Rotational tolerance criterion applies if the retro-reflector is marked TOP.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked device ±5° about its reference axis and verify that RI stays at or above the prescribed value throughout.

requirements.text: If the RI for β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0° exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, the retro-reflector shall meet the RI requirements with all measurements, for all illumination and divergence angles, made at ε = 0°.
requirements.why: Determines the orientation in which the retro-reflector's compliance is assessed.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, ε = 0°. If it is ≥150 % of the specified value, verify all angle combinations at ε = 0°.

requirements.text: For testing the retro-reflection, the retro-reflector shall be illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
requirements.why: Sets the illumination condition under which the retro-reflector's RI must comply.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the photometric RI test uses a CIE Standard Illuminant A source.

requirements.text: The RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured with a source angular diameter δ ≤ 10', a measuring device angular diameter γ ≤ 10' and an illuminated area angular diameter η ≤ 80'.
requirements.why: Measurement geometry condition under which the product's RI compliance is established.
requirements.test_case: Check the test geometry (source, receiver and sample angular sizes) against these limits before measurement.

requirements.text: The RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured at a distance that respects at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η, but not lower than 10 m.
requirements.why: Test condition constraining the RI verification of the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the test distance is ≥ 10 m and that the δ, γ and η limits are met.

requirements.text: The illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflector, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform, such that max/min ≤ 1.05.
requirements.why: Illumination uniformity condition under which the retro-reflector is tested.
requirements.test_case: Scan the illuminance over the device area with a sensor no larger than one-tenth of that area and verify that max/min ≤ 1.05.

requirements.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.
requirements.why: The product includes a rear retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) whose illuminating surface shape is constrained.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector illuminating surface from 10 m and confirm its shape cannot be easily confused with a triangle.

requirements.text: The moulded plastics retro-reflective device (Class IA/IB) shall be subjected to a heat resistance test of 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
requirements.why: The product's retro-reflector is a moulded PMMA rear retro-reflector of Class IA/IB, so it must withstand this heat conditioning.
requirements.test_case: Condition the retro-reflector in a dry oven at 65 °C ± 2 °C for 48 h, then cool for 1 h at 23 °C ± 2 °C before inspection.

requirements.text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component shall be visible.
requirements.why: This is the pass criterion for the heat resistance test of the product's moulded plastics retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the conditioned retro-reflector for cracks or appreciable distortion, especially of the prism optics.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. The test shall be repeated after turning the device through 180° so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water. The device shall then be immediately immersed under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
requirements.why: The product includes a retro-reflector integrated in the rear lamp, which must withstand the prescribed water immersion conditions.
requirements.test_case: Strip the retro-reflector of removable parts and immerse it at 50 °C ± 5 °C for 10 min in both orientations, then immediately at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

requirements.text: After the immersion test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
requirements.why: This is the pass/fail sealing criterion for the retro-reflector's optical unit (P-05) and its sealing.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the reflecting surface of the prism optics for water after immersion.

requirements.text: If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water, or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured by the method of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. after the device has been lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside, and shall meet the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector must still meet its RI photometric requirement after the water penetration test.
requirements.test_case: Shake off excess water and measure the RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, then compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.

requirements.text: During the water spray test, all drain holes and other openings of the retro-reflective device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
requirements.why: The rear lamp with integrated retro-reflector must be tested in its as-built venting and drainage configuration.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the test sample before the spray test to confirm drain holes and openings are open and any drain wicks are fitted.

requirements.text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF during the water spray test.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector is grouped with the rear position, stop and reversing lamps in this rear lamp.
requirements.test_case: Operate the rear position, stop and reversing lamps at design voltage on a 5 min ON / 55 min OFF cycle during the spray test.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall withstand a water spray test lasting 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min), with the device rotated about its vertical axis at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1, followed by a 1 hour drain period.
requirements.why: Defines the moisture exposure that the lamp's sealing and drainage must withstand.
requirements.test_case: Run the 12 h rotating water spray test at 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, then let the device drain for 1 h with the cabinet door closed.

requirements.text: Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the device, nor shall one be able to form by tapping or tilting the device.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion for the seal, gasket and drainage design of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp interior after draining, and tap and tilt it to check for any pooled water.

requirements.text: After the water spray test and after drying the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 and shall meet the prescribed values.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector's photometric performance must be maintained after moisture exposure.
requirements.test_case: Dry the exterior, then measure the RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 values.

requirements.text: During the dust exposure test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
requirements.why: The lamp must resist dust in its as-built venting configuration.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample before dust exposure to confirm its openings are unobstructed and any drain wicks are fitted.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall withstand exposure to test dust (fine powdered cement to ASTM C 150-84), agitated at intervals of 15 min for 2 to 15 s over a duration of 5 hours, with the device placed no closer than 150 mm from a chamber wall.
requirements.why: Defines the dust exposure that the lamp's sealing must resist without photometric degradation.
requirements.test_case: Expose the mounted lamp in the dust chamber for 5 h with periodic agitation.

requirements.text: Upon completion of the dust exposure test, after the exterior of the device has been cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and shall satisfy the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.why: Dust penetration must not significantly affect the photometric output of the integrated retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Clean and dry the exterior, then measure the RI at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° against the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall be so designed that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.
requirements.why: Durability design requirement applying to the rear retro-reflector (P-05) of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Perform the ISO 9227:2017 saline mist test, then re-measure photometry and colour against the prescribed limits.

requirements.text: The front surface of the retro-reflective device shall resist tarnishing and the protection of its rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly where an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.
requirements.why: Defines what the retro-reflector's front surface and rear face are checked for under corrosion exposure.
requirements.test_case: After the corrosion test, visually inspect the front surface for tarnishing and the rear face protection for deterioration.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
requirements.why: The retro-reflector is combined with the rear lamp, so the whole lamp is the test sample.
requirements.test_case: Expose the complete rear lamp, stripped of removable parts, to 2 x 24 h of saline mist with a 2 h drying interval.

requirements.text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
requirements.why: Pass/fail criterion of the corrosion test for the lamp with its integrated retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the lamp and retro-reflector immediately after the saline mist exposure for corrosion that impairs efficiency.

requirements.text: After the corrosion test, with the surface cleaned of salt deposits and after a recovery period of 48 hours, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas measured at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20' shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
requirements.why: Post-corrosion photometric criterion for the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Clean the salt deposits, allow 48 h recovery, then measure retro-reflection at β2 = 5°, α = 20' and compare with the limits.

requirements.text: When the outer surface of the retro-reflector, and in particular the illuminating surface, is lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol, the surface shall not show any apparent surface changes when inspected visually after about five minutes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
requirements.why: The product contains a moulded plastic (PMMA) retro-reflector, which is subject to the fuel resistance test of Annex 7 Part 1 paragraph 1.1.
requirements.test_case: Wipe the illuminating surface of the moulded PMMA retro-reflector with the n-heptane/toluol mixture. After about 5 minutes, inspect visually and confirm there are no apparent surface changes other than slight cracks.

requirements.text: After the outer surface of the moulded plastics retro-reflector (Class IA/IB), in particular the illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes, the retro-reflector shall have a coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) which, measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2., satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4. (verified at an angle of divergence of 20' and illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.).
requirements.why: The product includes a moulded PMMA retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) which must retain its photometric performance after lubricating oil exposure.
requirements.test_case: Wipe the illuminating surface with detergent lubricating oil, clean after ~5 min, then measure RI at 20' divergence and 0° illumination and compare with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.

requirements.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.why: [recall pass]
requirements.test_case: Inspect the ESA and confirm the approval mark is at the location given on the approval communication form and is conspicuous and accessible.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA representative of this type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED PCB is an ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, so its conducted transient immunity must be verified by these methods.
requirements.test_case: Check that the ESA conducted transient immunity test report covers the ISO 16750-2 starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b per Annex 10.

requirements.text: The starting profile shall be assessed according to the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1, and the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) of ISO 7637-1 shall be applied for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This sets the pass/fail classification scheme the lamp ESA must meet under conducted transients.
requirements.test_case: Review the test plan and report to confirm the ESA pass/fail evaluation uses the ISO 16750-1 classes for the starting profile and the ISO 7637-1 FPSC for the pulses.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED PCB is an ESA, and this constant upper-band broadband emission limit applies to it.
requirements.test_case: Measure ESA broadband radiated emissions per Annex 7 between 400 and 1,000 MHz and confirm all values are below 63 dB microvolts/m.

requirements.text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED module PCB is an ESA, so its narrowband emissions in the 400–1,000 MHz band must stay under this fixed limit.
requirements.test_case: Measure the LED PCB ESA's narrowband radiated emissions per Annex 8 from 400 to 1,000 MHz and confirm all values are below 53 dBµV/m.

requirements.text: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
requirements.why: [recall pass] x
requirements.test_case: Check the spectrum analyser settings in the test report: VBW ≥ 3 × RBW for peak scans.

requirements.text: FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a distinct condition on how the ESA's narrowband emission compliance is measured, and the first reader merged it.
requirements.test_case: Review the FFT receiver configuration and test log to confirm continuous recording and evaluation during each measurement period.

requirements.text: If FFT-based instruments are used, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a separate numeric test-condition constraint on the ESA emission verification, and the first reader merged it.
requirements.test_case: Check the FFT instrument settings and record to confirm a measurement time of at least 1 s per analysis band.

requirements.text: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video band width shall be at least three times the resolution band width (RBW).
requirements.why: [recall pass] This measurement condition constrains the ESA emission test result and was omitted by the first reader.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the spectrum analyser setup that VBW is at least 3 × RBW for peak measurements.

requirements.text: The ESA narrowband emission test shall be performed at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz (or alternatively at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each of the 14 defined frequency bands).
requirements.why: [recall pass] This defines the frequency coverage over which the ESA must be shown to meet the emission limits.
requirements.test_case: Confirm in the test report that the frequency scan intervals follow CISPR 12 over 30–1,000 MHz, or that the 14 highest-emission frequencies per band were tested.

requirements.text: The ESA shall limit the conducted transients it generates on the vehicle power supply.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The lamp's LED PCB is an ESA connected to the vehicle supply, so its conducted transient emissions must be limited separately from its immunity.
requirements.test_case: Measure the transient emissions on the ESA supply lines according to ISO 7637-2 and compare them with the applicable limits.

requirements.text: If it is not practicable to keep the apparent surface of the rear position lamps and retro-reflectors from being hidden more than 50 per cent by a movable component, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for these lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies to the rear position lamp and retro-reflector when installed near or on movable components.
requirements.test_case: Move the component to each fixed open position and check that the additional lamps switch ON and meet the position, visibility, colour and photometric requirements.

requirements.text: Where additional lamps for the rear position lamp or rear retro-reflector functions are fitted and switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies to rear position lamp and retro-reflector functions mounted on movable components such as a tailgate.
requirements.test_case: Open the movable component and measure the additional lamps against the position, visibility and photometric requirements.

requirements.text: Where rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control and are combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, their intensities shall vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies if the rear position and stop lamp functions use variable intensity control.
requirements.test_case: Trigger the variable intensity conditions and measure the rear position and stop lamp intensities together to verify proportional variation.

requirements.text: Where rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 have variable luminous intensity control, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of the two lamps shall be maintained throughout variation transitions over the entire intensity range.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies to the stop and position functions if they have variable intensity.
requirements.test_case: Measure the stop-to-position intensity ratio across the whole dimming range and during transitions.

requirements.text: Where variable intensity control responds to traffic conditions, a decrease of the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp and stop lamp, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, shall only be activated when the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal to or less than 20 m. An intensity decrease already activated may remain active only as long as the vehicle speed is equal to or less than 50 km/h.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a constraint on the variable intensity behaviour of the R2/S2 functions, if fitted.
requirements.test_case: Vary the vehicle speed and following distance and check when the intensity decrease activates and deactivates.

requirements.text: No sharp variation of luminous intensity of the variable intensity rear position lamp and stop lamp shall be observed during transition.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies to the variable intensity rear position and stop lamp functions, if fitted.
requirements.test_case: Record the intensity over time during a dimming transition and check that there are no abrupt steps.

requirements.text: Where the rear lamps incorporate a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo shall be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and any logo shall be a vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logo.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies if the rear lamp design incorporates a logo.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the rear lamps on the vehicle for the number and ownership of logos.

requirements.text: Where the rear lamp light-signalling functions incorporate a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a conditional approval obligation on the light-signalling lamp if it carries a logo.
requirements.test_case: Check the approval documentation and marking for R148 approval covering the logo lamp.

requirements.text: Where the stop lamp is grouped with direction-indicator lamps, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The stop lamp of this rear lamp may be grouped with direction indicators on the vehicle rear, which constrains the colour-area layout.
requirements.test_case: Project the apparent surfaces onto a plane perpendicular to the reference axis and check that no horizontal or vertical line crosses more than two colour borderlines.

requirements.text: Where the stop lamp is grouped with direction-indicator lamps, their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, based upon the areas bounded by the outline of their light emitting surfaces, shall not overlap.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a geometric constraint on the stop lamp's apparent surface when it is grouped with direction indicators.
requirements.test_case: Check the drawing or photograph along the reference axis to confirm that the stop lamp and direction-indicator apparent surfaces do not overlap.

requirements.text: Where a single lamp as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(b) or (c) is composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors, it shall be installed such that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro-reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing these projections, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This applies if the rear position lamp, stop lamp or retro-reflector function is realised as two "D" lamps or two independent retro-reflectors.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected apparent surfaces and check either the 60 per cent fill ratio of the circumscribing quadrilateral or an edge gap of 75 mm or less.

requirements.text: Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1.(d) (interdependent lamp systems) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This binds any lamp function of the product that is realised as an interdependent lamp system.
requirements.test_case: For an interdependent lamp system, verify either the 60 per cent apparent-surface fill ratio or the 75 mm maximum gap between distinct parts.

requirements.text: In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies if any of the rear lamp functions are made up as an interdependent lamp system, which this section does not exclude.
requirements.test_case: With all interdependent lamps of the system switched on together, verify the prescribed angles of geometric visibility are met for the installed lamp system.

requirements.text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED lamp may use an external electronic control gear that would need its own marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect any external control gear of the LED lamp for its identification number and manufacturer name.

requirements.text: If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The lamp has a separate outer lens sealed to the housing, so the marking location depends on whether the lens is detachable.
requirements.test_case: Check the design for lens detachability; if detachable, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.

requirements.text: In case an outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The outer lens covers several functions (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector), which may be approved as separate devices.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the main body of each device sharing the outer lens and confirm it carries only the marking of its own functions.

requirements.text: In the case of a lamp with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.
requirements.why: [recall pass] x
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp at the applicant-specified supply conditions during photometric tests and confirm compliance.

requirements.text: Where a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp function, all requirements of this Regulation for that specific lamp function shall still be fulfilled with the logo present.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Fulfilling all function requirements is a separate condition from the one-logo limit, and the first reader merged the two.
requirements.test_case: Carry out photometric and colorimetric tests on the lamp function containing the logo and verify that all requirements for that function are met.

requirements.text: Where the stop lamp is of category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically in case of failure of the variable intensity control.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The product has a stop lamp; if it is a variable-intensity S2 lamp, its failure behaviour is a separate obligation from that of the rear position lamp.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control of the S2 stop lamp and measure that the luminous intensity automatically falls within the steady-intensity requirements of the respective category.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Binds the lamp design if any function uses replaceable approved light sources; LED replaceability is still to be confirmed.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to insert the light source in all possible orientations and confirm that only the correct position is achievable.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, applying the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a holder construction requirement on the lamp when replaceable approved light sources are used.
requirements.test_case: Gauge the holder dimensions against the relevant IEC 60061 holder data sheet.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the light source holder shall also conform to the IEC 60061 holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s).
requirements.why: [recall pass] This adds a holder conformity condition when LED substitute light sources are prescribed for the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Gauge the holder against the IEC 60061 holder data sheet for the prescribed LED substitute category.

requirements.text: Where a variable intensity control is used, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Applies to the stop/rear position lamp functions if they are driven at variable intensity.
requirements.test_case: Operate the lamp through the full range of variable intensity control signals and verify that the measured intensities stay within the paragraph 5 range.

requirements.text: Where a variable intensity control is used, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp: (a) under night-time conditions, for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions; (b) under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, and clean lens), for other systems.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Limits the maximum intensity of the variable-intensity stop/rear position lamp functions.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity under night-time or standard-condition control signals and compare it with the steady maximum in paragraph 5.

requirements.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall comply with the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The stop lamp P-02 is the S1 category for M1, and its light distribution must follow the Table 7 row for S1.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at the grid points of Figure A3-I, compared against the required percentages of the minimum on-axis intensity.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the category S1 (steady) stop lamp shall emit a minimum luminous intensity of 3∙10^-1 cd.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is the minimum intensity across the visibility field that applies to the stop lamp function present on the product.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity at the boundary directions of the Table A2-1 geometric visibility field and verify each value is ≥ 0.3 cd.

requirements.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The LED stop lamp must meet the failure provisions stated for the stop lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of LED light sources and check the lamp behaviour against paragraph 4.6.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The colour requirement applies directly to the stop lamp's emitted light through the red outer lens.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of the emitted light and verify they fall within the red boundaries.

requirements.text: Where the reversing lamp type approval is granted applying the condition of verification only up to 30° inwards, the reversing lamp shall only be installed on a vehicle in a pair of devices.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The approval condition restricts how the AR lamp may be installed on the M1 vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Check the communication form (item 9.1.3) and the vehicle installation drawings to confirm that the lamp is fitted only as a pair.

requirements.text: Where equivalent methods are used, with the consent of the competent authority, in a conformity test of the lamp carried out by the manufacturer, those methods shall be proven equivalent to the methods laid down in this Regulation.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a borderline procedural obligation: any alternative conformity-of-production test method used on this lamp must be shown equivalent before its results count.
requirements.test_case: Review the equivalence justification and correlation data for any alternative conformity test method against the Regulation's reference method.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of the retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
requirements.why: [recall pass] The product includes a Class IA/IB retro-reflector, which must keep its optical properties stable over time.
requirements.test_case: Run the Part 3 of Annex 4 stability-in-time test on two samples, then verify colour and RI.

requirements.text: The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum RI values after the heat resistance test shall meet the complete photometric requirements of paragraph 5.1.4.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Full photometric compliance must hold across the production spread of the retro-reflector.
requirements.test_case: Select the samples with minimum and maximum RI at 20'/0° and perform complete photometry against Table 3 values for red Class IA/IB.

requirements.text: After the stability in time test (Part 3 of Annex 4) and after the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6), the retro-reflector shall meet colorimetry (visual inspection or trichromatic coordinates) and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Table 4 for Class IA/IB sets the colour and photometry pass criteria after the ageing tests.
requirements.test_case: After the stability and weathering tests, measure chromaticity and RI at 20' divergence and 0°/0° illumination.

requirements.text: The CIE-angular system as shown in Figure A4-I shall be used for specifying and measuring the retro-reflector.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Defines the angular reference frame in which the retro-reflector's RI compliance is specified and verified.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the test report specifies the retro-reflector angles (α, β1, β2, ε) in the CIE angular system.

requirements.text: The residual stray light value, measured with the sample covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape, or a suitably oriented specular black surface with a light trap, shall be subtracted from the value measured on the retro-reflector.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Determines the corrected RI value of the retro-reflector that must meet the photometric limits.
requirements.test_case: Measure stray light with the retro-reflector covered and check that this value is subtracted from the measured RI before comparing against the limits.

requirements.text: During the water spray test, the retro-reflective device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a separate test condition that the rear retro-reflector must withstand; the first reader merged it into the test-duration requirement.
requirements.test_case: Verify the rotating platform speed during the water spray test is within 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

requirements.text: After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed before evaluation.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a distinct drain-period condition that sets when the absence of a water pool is assessed; the first reader merged it into the duration requirement.
requirements.test_case: Check that the device drains for 1 h with the cabinet door closed before inspecting it for standing water.

requirements.text: The retro-reflective device shall be subjected to a water spray with a precipitation rate at the device of 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, measured with a vertical cylindrical collector 100 mm high with a minimum inside diameter of 140 mm.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This sets the severity of water exposure under which the retro-reflector's sealing and RI must remain compliant.
requirements.test_case: Measure the precipitation rate with the specified collector before the spray test and confirm it is within 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min.

requirements.text: Where the retro-reflective device has a length exceeding 600 mm, it shall be horizontally centred in the dust test chamber during the dust exposure test.
requirements.why: [recall pass] This is a conditional dust-test placement constraint that depends on the dimensions of the product.
requirements.test_case: Measure the device length and check its position in the dust chamber.

requirements.text: In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the device shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
requirements.why: [recall pass] Sets the corrosion test condition the retro-reflector or combined lamp must survive if it contains essential metal components.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the retro-reflector has essential metal components; if so, run the salt-spray test at 35 °C ± 2 °C with 5 % NaCl solution per ISO 9227:2017.
